title: First run: with no engine, Archipelia offers to set one up and gets it ready
covers: Engine first-run dialog, install and engine test
context: With no engine, Archipelia offers to set one up. The first-run dialog shows a release picker with the newest stable release selected and what will be installed. Install runs the setup and the engine test until the engine is ready. A default install now records the release tag it installed.
changed: hooks/engine-startup: the first-run dialog with the release picker
packages/catalog: a default install is downloaded by the tag it records, and an engine switch keeps that tag when it fits

setup.label: engine
setup.text: Way A: close Archipelia, rename the folder Data\engine to engine-keep, then launch. The dialog opens by itself. Way B: keep the ready engine and remove it in steps 2 and 3 (this deletes its files).

setup.label: network
setup.text: Needed. The release list comes from GitHub and the install downloads about 90 MB.

setup.label: order
setup.text: Run this test before the test Engine: a newer version is offered once. That one starts from the engine this one installs.

setup.label: data
setup.text: The .user-data\Data folder inside the bundle-4 worktree (X:\archipelia\.worktrees\bundle-4\.user-data\Data).

steps: Launch with the command of this test. If the welcome tour opens, press Skip. With way A the dialog Set up the engine is already open: go to step 4.
Way B: in the sidebar, under App, press Engine. In Installed engines, press the trash icon on the row tagged Active (its name starts with Remove Archipelago).
A confirmation titled Delete Archipelago X with Python Y opens. It says no session can be made or hosted until you install an engine. Press Remove.
The dialog Set up the engine opens on its own. The newest stable release is selected, and the facts list Archipelago, Python, Requirements and Download (About 90 MB).
Press Ins On the Engine page watch the Status bar named Engine s
Every step passes: Check the versions, Download Python, Download Archipelago, Install the requirements, Pack the official worlds, Carry your worlds, Test the engine, Switch to it.
When the Status line reads Ready, Installed engines lists the new engine with the tag Active.
Close Archipelia completely and launch it again with the same command. The dialog Set up the engine must not come back.
pass: Removing the active engine opens Set up the engine on its own, right after the confirmation.
The newest stable release is preselected, and the facts list Archipelago, Python, Requirements and Download.
Install runs every step, including Pack the official worlds and Test the engine, and ends with Status Ready.
After a restart the dialog does not appear again.
fail: No dialog appears after Remove, the picker is empty, or the preselected release is not the newest stable one.
A setup step fails, the setup hangs, or Status stays Setting up, Setup failed or Not set up.
The dialog comes back on the next start although the engine is ready.
notes: Way A exists because a bundle ships with a ready engine. Delete engine-keep afterwards if you do not want it.
Optional: press Not now instead of Install in the dialog. Engine then shows Not set up with a Set up engine button in Status.
Optional, network off: the dialog says it could not read the release list and offers only the version Archipelia was tested with.
The trash icon is greyed out while a session of that engine runs. Close the session tab and stop the room first.
